facts.text: Matlock’s official founding in 1888 came after the Illinois Central Railroad extended a branch line through Grant Township, opening the prairie to farmers.
The town was originally called Maurice but was renamed Matlock after the English hometown of early settler Robert Allen, reflecting British roots.
A German Baptist congregation formed in 1885, illustrating the diverse ethnic mix that helped shape Matlock’s early community.
The first Presbyterian church built in 1888 later became a Baptist church, underscoring religion’s role in community cohesion.
Matlock incorporated as a city on July 5, 1897, solidifying its status as a self-governing rural hub.
In April 2024, an EF1 tornado struck about four miles west-northwest of Matlock, damaging outbuildings but leaving no injuries.
